Empirical Research Plan: “The Effect of Public Report Cards on Health-Care Providers’ Performance and Patient Outcomes”

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------------
Preferred strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) combined with an event-study (two-way fixed-effects).

Why appropriate  
• Treatment (public report cards) is a policy shock that can be dated precisely.  
• Some providers are exposed while others are not (e.g. specialties not yet covered, neighbouring region, or facilities below the minimum‐volume threshold that were exempt).  
• We observe multiple periods before and after ⇒ we can test pre-trends and dynamics.  

We will estimate:  
Y_it = α_i + λ_t + β Treat_i × Post_t + X′_it γ + ε_it  
and the analogous event-time specification.

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treat_i = 1 for providers whose performance was newly disclosed in the first wave of report cards (e.g. cardiac surgeons, hospitals above threshold, Region A). 0 otherwise.

Control group (counterfactual)  
Providers not exposed during the sample window—e.g.  
• Specialties/hospitals in the same region whose outcomes continued to be undisclosed, or  
• Providers in an otherwise similar neighbouring region where rollout occurred later.

Treatment timing / event date  
Post_t = 1 for all periods t ≥ Q3-2016 (exact quarter when cards were first posted online); 0 before.

If a staggered rollout is actually available we will generalise to share-weighted TWFE or Sun-Abraham estimators.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of report cards, treated and control providers would have followed the same trend in performance/outcomes.  
Plausibility: Providers face the same reimbursement schedule, regulation, and macro-trends; only transparency differs. Pre-trend tests and placebo leads inside the event-study will be reported.

A2. No spillovers: Publication of treated providers’ scores does not change behaviour of the control group.  
Plausibility: Could be violated if patients shift across providers. We will test for demand reallocation (volumes) and, if present, instrument outcomes with lagged own treatment only.

A3. Stable composition: Entry/exit of providers is not driven by the policy in a way that biases results.  
Plausibility: Short-run exit unlikely because licensing is sticky; we will include balanced and unbalanced panels and show robustness.

A4. No simultaneous confounders: No other policy exactly coincides with Q3-2016 that differentially affects treated.  
We will search policy archives and include specialty-specific trends.

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
------------------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1: Differential pre-trends.  
• Mitigation: Plot event-study coefficients (–8 to –1). Add provider-specific linear trends as robustness. Use synthetic control matching on pre-period performance.

Threat 2: Patient sorting or competitive spillovers.  
• Mitigation: Estimate intent-to-treat (provider fixed) and “own-outcome/others-outcome” models. Control for patient mix; alternatively instrument actual patient volume with lagged policy exposure.

Threat 3: Measurement error in performance metrics (learning curve).  
• Mitigation: Use risk-adjusted outcome rates published by the regulator; winsorise outliers; instrument noisy performance with jack-knifed leave-one-out measures.

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)

# 1. Data ------------------------------------------------------------------
prov <- read_csv("provider_panel.csv")   # one row per provider–quarter

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------------------
prov <- prov %>%
  mutate(post       = (quarter >= "2016 Q3"),
         treat      = if_else(specialty %in% c("Cardiac", "Vascular"), 1, 0),
         treat_post = treat * post,
         time_to    = as.integer(quarter - as.yearqtr("2016 Q3")))  # event time

# 3. Main DID specification ------------------------------------------------
did_main <- feols(outcome_rate ~ treat_post + covariate1 + covariate2 |
                  provider_id + quarter, data = prov, cluster = ~provider_id)

etable(did_main, title = "Main DID: Report-Card Effect")

# 4. Event-study (dynamic) -------------------------------------------------
es <- feols(outcome_rate ~ i(time_to, treat, ref = -1) + covariate1 + covariate2 |
            provider_id + quarter, data = prov, cluster = ~provider_id)

iplot(es, main = "Event-Study Coefficients")

# 5. Robustness: alternative control group --------------------------------
alt <- prov %>% filter(region == "Adjacent_NoPolicy")
did_alt <- feols(outcome_rate ~ treat_post + covariate1 + covariate2 |
                 provider_id + quarter, data = alt, cluster = ~provider_id)

etable(list("Main" = did_main, "Alt control" = did_alt),
       title = "Robustness: Alternative Control")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory suggests transparency raises reputational stakes, leading providers to invest in quality. Prior: β < 0 for adverse-event rates (≈ –5 % relative decline) and β > 0 for positive process metrics (≈ +3 % relative rise). Heterogeneity: larger effects for low-baseline performers.

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)

C1: Parallel trends supported by pre-period data ……… 1  
C2: No spillovers/interference ………………………………… 0 (some concern)  
C3: No anticipatory behaviour ………………………………… 1  
C4: Stable composition of treatment & control ………… 1  
C5: No other coincident shocks ……………………………… 0 (some concern)

Total = 3 / 5 – acceptable but demands robustness work.
